task.title: Define pages
task.shortdesc: Use an @page rule to set the size, margins and other properties of the pages in the PDF.

info.p: An @page rule has an optional list of page selectors, separated by commas, and a block of declarations:

The first rule has no selector and applies to every page. The second applies to pages that match either selector. A selector is an optional page type name followed by page pseudo-classes, with no white space between them.
A block can contain page properties, the size descriptor, and page-margin rules.

step.cmd: Set the page size with size

info.p: The size descriptor sets the size of the page. Its initial value is auto, which gives an A4 page.

ul.li: A page size name, such as A4, selects a standard sheet.
portrait puts the shorter sides horizontal and landscape puts the longer sides horizontal. Use one of them with a name, or alone to orient the default A4 sheet.
One length sets the width and the height, which gives a square page.
Two lengths set the width and then the height. A length cannot be negative.

info.p: These are the page size names:
The sizes are width by height, in portrait orientation.
Page margins are the space between the edge of the page and the page area, where the content of the document is placed. If you do not set a margin, it is 1in.
The margin property sets all four margins. It takes one to four values, which are lengths, percentages or auto:

ul.li: One value sets all four sides.
Two values set the top and bottom, then the right and left.
Three values set the top, then the left and right, then the bottom.
Four values set the top, right, bottom and left, in that order.

info.p: A percentage is a fraction of the page width for the left and right margins, and of the page height for the top and bottom margins.
Use margin-top, margin-right, margin-bottom and margin-left to set one side. For example, use wider inner margins in a two-sided document:
A page selector chooses the pages that a rule applies to, by page type or by position.
A page type name matches the pages that get that name from the page property. For example, @page wide matches the pages of type wide. Names are case-sensitive.

ul.li: :left and :right match left and right pages. In a document that is read left to right, the first page is a right page.
:blank matches the empty pages that forced page breaks produce.
:nth(An+B) matches pages by their position in the document. :nth(2n) selects pages 2, 4, 6 and so on, and :nth(3n+1) selects pages 1, 4, 7 and so on.

info.p: Add of and a page type to count only the pages of one page group, as in :nth(1 of chapter). An element that has a named page and a forced page break starts a new page group.

step.cmd: Assign a page type with page

info.p: The page property gives the pages of an element a page type. Its value is auto or a name that you also use in an @page rule.
With auto, an element takes the page type of its nearest ancestor that has a name. A box with a different page type than the page before it starts on a new page.

A page-margin rule is an at-rule inside an @page rule, such as @top-center or @bottom-right. Each one defines a box in the margin. The box appears only if its content property has a value other than none or normal. Use counter(page) to show the page number.
